newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo says most losing copper positions covered.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo says most losing copper positions covered.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp has liquidated most of its open, uncovered copper positions, although it still has some long and short positions in the market, Sumitomo president Kenji Miyahara told a news conference on Thursday.
"As a result of our liquidation up to now, there still remain some positions, including both short and long positions, but the liquidation of uncovered positions is nearly complete," he said.
"Accordingly, there is almost no risk remaining and it is our judgment that we will not again revise the estimated loss we have announced today," he added.
"We hope you will understand that this is the result of our doing the very best we could to liquidate (positions) under very difficult circumstances," he said.

He added that all of the unauthorised trading by dismissed Sumitomo chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, which the trade house blamed for its losses, was conducted on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and did not involve transactions in physical metal.
He also said Sumitomo had no plans to cut back its trading activity on the LME in the wake of the losses.
Sumitomo announced on Thursday it had revised upward its estimated losses from unauthorised copper trading to $2.6 billion from an original estimate of $1.8 billion announced on June 13.
Miyahara told a news conference the company had consulted with overseas regulators as it liquidated the positions, although he declined to give further details.

He also said that of the $2.6 billion loss, $1.2 billion was due to steep drops in copper prices earlier this year, first when Hamanaka was moved from his job as chief trader in May and then again when Sumitomo announced its losses and Hamanaka's firing in mid-June.
